1. Suppose a random variable $X$ can take values $\{1, 2, 3\}$ according to the probabilities $\{0.2, 0.3, 0.5\}$. You want to simulate values from this distribution using only random draws from a uniform distribution on $(0,1)$.

    Which of the following is the correct rule?

    - [ ] If $U < 0.2$, set $X = 1$; if $0.2 \le U < 0.5$, set $X = 2$; otherwise set $X = 3$.
    - [ ] If $U < 0.3$, set $X = 1$; if $0.3 \le U < 0.8$, set $X = 2$; otherwise set $X = 3$.
    - [ ] If $U < 0.5$, set $X = 1$; if $0.5 \le U < 0.8$, set $X = 2$; otherwise set $X = 3$.
    - [ ] If $U < 0.2$, set $X = 3$; if $0.2 \le U < 0.5$, set $X = 2$; otherwise set $X = 1$.


2. There is a $2\%$ click rate for an online advertisement. Suppose the number of people who click among the next $100$ people follows a binomial distribution.

    Which of the following is correct?

    - [ ] The parameters are $n = 0.02$ and $p = 100$.
    - [ ] The parameters are $n = 100$ and $p = 2$.
    - [ ] The parameters are $n = 100$ and $p = 0.02$.
    - [ ] The parameters are $n = 2$ and $p = 0.01$.

    Which of the following is a necessary assumption for the binomial model here?

    - [ ] Each person clicks independently with the same probability of clicking.
    - [ ] The probability of clicking changes after each person clicks.
    - [ ] The number of clicks must be exactly 50.
    - [ ] The click rate must be larger than 50% for the model to be valid.


3. Consider the number of times you roll a 6 in five rolls of a BIASED die.  Which of the following is correct? 

    - [ ] The model is binomial with $n = 6$ and $p = 0.5$.
    - [ ] The model is binomial with $n = 5$ and $p = 6$.
    - [ ] The model is binomial with $n = 5$ and $p$ not given in the problem.
    - [ ] We cannot use a binomial model because the die is biased.

    Which model was used to approxmiate the number of hits in each of the small squares?

    - [ ] Uniform
    - [ ] Binomial
    - [ ] Poisson
    - [ ] Normal
